beginner.summary: For developers who know HTTP and one programming language and are new to real-time communication. Covers why polling, SSE and WebSocket exist, the RFC 6455 handshake, frames, opcodes and masking, the browser WebSocket API, text and binary messages, close codes, inspecting traffic, Node.js servers with ws, broadcasting and rooms, heartbeats, reconnection with backoff, message design, subprotocols, Socket.IO basics, Python and Java servers, NGINX proxying, TLS and Origin checks, testing, and a real-time chat capstone.
prerequisites: Writes working code in JavaScript, Python or Java and runs it from a terminal
Understands HTTP requests, response status codes and headers
Has Node.js 22 or later, a Chromium or Firefox browser and permission to install npm packages and Docker
outcomes: Explain the handshake and frame format of RFC 6455 and read them in a packet capture
Build WebSocket servers and clients in Node.js, Python and Java with correct close codes and heartbeats
Design reconnecting clients and typed messages that survive disconnects
Deliver a tested chat application behind NGINX with TLS, Origin checks and size limits
